decisions.title: Release rule A: ship if better than live
decisions.words: A, B, and C together please.
decisions.where: critic/RUBRIC.md §3; critic/policy.json release block; shipVerdict and validateReport in tools/critic-policy.mjs; tests/unit/critic-release-rules.test.ts. A build deploys when its reviewed changed area has no critical defect introduced or left reachable by the change and no regression against the live build; majors that are not regressions are disclosed in the release announcement and carried into the next batch; defects inside a brand-new feature do not block, and that feature may ship switched off; unknown on a critical is a HOLD. Asked after two candidates in a row were held for a day by the pre-deploy deep review although each was better than the live build.

decisions.title: Release rule B: the deep review runs after the deploy

A shared-system change needs a focused review of the production candidate before the deploy and its deep review afterwards on the live build, where it stays that build's obligation and its issue list drives the next batch. Deep-before-deploy survives only for the save-data class (src/app/SaveData.ts, save schema or migration) and a milestone claim; at most two deploys may go out while a deep review is owed, the third refuses. The finished-milestone standard is unchanged.

resolutions.what: A one-time, idempotent migration in the save loader: a save whose settings carry no ffx2AtbMigrated marker gets ffx2Atb 'wait' and the marker, whatever ffx2Atb held (Active was the only behaviour before, so nobody chose it); a marked save keeps the player's choice; a fresh save is Wait with the marker; nothing else in the save changes. Save-data class: a deep review of the candidate before deploy. FFX-2 only.

Keep the whole-menu hold in this release; build the faithful split (the clock runs at the top-level command window, freezes in a submenu; research/ffx2-combat-core.md §1.5, [single source]) in the next release. Nothing built here. FFX-2 only.

B + C: the briefing's fourth line is mode-aware, read when the briefing is shown (first launch, title replay, pause replay). Bailey's approved line 'In hers, the clock does not wait' shows only when Settings.ffx2Atb is 'active'; under 'wait' the agent-drafted line 'In hers, the clock holds while you choose' shows (true of the build: the engine moves nothing while a command menu is open). The Wait wording is INFERRED, awaiting his yes (docs/target/targets.json, tile 'Onboarding C1', reaction.inferred). src/ui/coach/coachCopy.ts BRIEFING_WAIT_LINE / briefingLines, Briefing.ts.
